config.title: Multi-Step Form

intro.title: Multi-Step Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a multi-step form that guides users through a sign-up process across several screens, like entering personal details and preferences. You'll learn how to manage the current step using React state, conditionally render different form sections, and validate user input between steps. The main technologies used are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and React hooks like useState to track the form's progress. By the end, you'll have a working form that navigates through steps while maintaining user data.
intro.usecase: Multi-step forms are a foundational UI pattern for breaking complex data entry into manageable chunks, improving user experience and completion rates. You'll encounter them in real-world products like e-commerce checkouts (shipping, billing, review), account creation wizards, and complex settings panels. As a developer, implementing this pattern requires managing step state, validation per step, and navigation logic—skills essential for building polished, user-friendly applications.

objectives: Implement a multi-step form component using React and TypeScript
Configure state management to track the current step and form data
Construct navigation controls to move between form steps
Initialize and update form validation for each step
Render conditional UI elements based on the active step
Bind form inputs to state and handle user input changes
Integrate a submission handler to process the completed form data

steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to add the return type annotation after the parameter list.

// Create the MultiStepForm component here

steps.title: Create next step handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleNextStep inside your MultiStepForm component that increments the currentStep state when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCurrentStep with the current step value plus one.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleNextStep function is added to the component that will advance the form to the next step when triggered.
successCriteria: The handleNextStep function is defined and calls setCurrentStep with currentStep + 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it increments currentStep by calling setCurrentStep.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleNextStep function isn't defined correctly. It should increment currentStep when called.

steps.title: Create previous step handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handlePreviousStep inside your component that decrements the currentStep state by 1 when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setCurrentStep to update the state. You can decrement by using the previous step value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handlePreviousStep function that decreases currentStep by 1 when invoked.
successCriteria: The handlePreviousStep function is defined and uses setCurrentStep to decrement the step value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly decrements the currentStep state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handlePreviousStep function is missing or doesn't properly decrement the step. Try using setCurrentStep with the previous value.
